summary: Looks up a named resource via sub_497AD0 using context this+4. On success, allocates a 52-byte node through OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper, initializes it via the sub_499B10 constructor, fills slots with caller arguments a2-a5 and the lookup result, optionally overrides four slots from the resource's indirect data when a7 is set, then links the node either into a named node's child list (when a9 matches an existing list node) or into the main list anchored at this+8, incrementing the counter at this+0xC. On lookup failure with a8 set, formats an error message and shows a MessageBoxA. Returns the new node or 0.

operations.description: Guard on the name argument a6 being non-null; a null name returns 0 immediately.
Call sub_497AD0 with the context pointer at this+4, the name a6, and a zero flag to look up the resource.
Guard on the lookup result being non-null; on failure, if a8 is set the function reports the error and returns 0.
Call OperatorNewNhMallocWrapper with size 52 to allocate the new node.
Call sub_499B10 on the allocated memory to construct/initialize the node; result is null if allocation failed.
Populate node slots from arguments: slot 1 = a5, slot 3 = a3, slot 0 = a4, slot 2 = a2, slot 9 = 0, slot 8 = lookup result.
When a7 is set, override slots 2 and 0 to 0 and copy slots 1 and 3 from the resource's indirect data at (*(v11+12) + 28) and (*(v11+12) + 32).
Guard on a9 being non-null and the main list head at this+8 being non-null: selects the named-sub-list path that walks nodes by their slot 9 pointer to locate a9.

When a9 is found in the main list: increment a9 slot 4, copy a9 slot 6 into the new node slot 6, and append the new node to a9's child list via slot 10 pointers (walk to the tail if the child list is non-empty).

Otherwise append the new node to the main list anchored at this+8: walk nodes by their +36-byte next pointer to the tail and set the tail's next pointer at +36, then increment the counter at this+0xC; if the list was empty, make the new node the head and set the count.
Lookup-failure path: when a8 is set, format the message with StringFormatWithBufferOverflowCheck and show a MessageBoxA with the OptionsFrame title string; otherwise fail silently.
Return the new node pointer, or 0 when the name was null or the lookup failed.
